Perceptual solidification operates as a kernel convolution of actual and revived sensory states, forming a coherent object representation. This process enables the mind to bridge immediate sensation with stored experience, yielding a unified cognitive object. The integration mechanism implies a dual structure: one for present sensory input and another for recalled sensations. The resulting percept is not a simple sum but a structured synthesis. In GSI, this maps to Bayesian belief updates where priors (memories) are combined with likelihoods (sensory data) to produce posterior beliefs. In GSE, it corresponds to a state transition function that evolves from raw sensory inputs to structured environmental models. The failure mode occurs when either sensory or memory components are corrupted or misaligned, leading to perceptual hallucinations or misidentifications.
